Run a time series model for a single geographic unit One-stage POOLED time-series version of condPois_1stage().

timeseries_1stage_glm.Rd

Run a time series model for a single geographic unit One-stage POOLED time-series version of condPois_1stage().

Usage

timeseries_1stage_glm(
  exposure_matrix,
  outcomes_tbl,
  argvar = NULL,
  arglag = NULL,
  maxlag = NULL,
  min_n = 50,
  time_trend = c("annual", "season"),
  dfseas = 7,
  df_time = NULL,
  population_col = NULL,
  add_dow = TRUE,
  global_cen = NULL,
  multi_zone = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  truncate = 0.025
)

Arguments

exposure_matrix

a matrix of exposures, with columns for lag, usually created by make_exposure_matrix

outcomes_tbl

a data.table of outcomes, created by make_outcome_table; must have date mapping

argvar

a list containing the argvar components for the crossbasis

arglag

a list containing the arglag components for the crossbasis

maxlag

an integer of the maximum lag

min_n

an integer describing the minimum number of cases for a single geo_unit

time_trend

one of "annual" or "season". "annual" (default) fits a single smooth spline over calendar date (ns(time_num, df = df_time)) and is appropriate for continuous, full-year daily data. "season" is for data that has been subset to a recurring part of the year (e.g., summer, or time_subset = list(month = 5:9) in make_outcome_table()/ make_exposure_matrix()) - calendar date jumps discontinuously between seasons/years in that case, so "season" instead fits factor(year) (to soak up inter-annual variation) plus a smooth spline over day-of-season (ns(day_of_season, df = df_time), which restarts each year and captures the within-season shape of the trend, shared across years).

dfseas

degrees of freedom PER YEAR OF DATA for the "annual" time trend spline. Default 7 (standard, see: Gasparrini). Ignored if df_time is supplied directly, and ignored entirely when time_trend = "season" (see df_time).

df_time

degrees of freedom for the time-trend spline. Meaning depends on time_trend: for "annual" this is the total df for ns(date, df = df_time) and if null is computed as round(dfseas * n_years). For "season" this is the df for the within-season smooth, ns(day_of_season, df = df_time), and if null defaults to 4.

population_col

optional name of a population column in outcomes_tbl, used as an offset; see add_population_offset()

add_dow

logical, whether to add factor(dow) to the model as another time trend adjustment. Default TRUE. #' @param population_col optional, can be incorporated as population offset if that data is available

global_cen

global centering point

multi_zone

must be true

verbose

used to print crossbasis args the first time

truncate

proportion of the exposure distribution to trim from each tail when choosing the centering point (passed to get_centered_cp)

Value

a timeseries_1stage model object

Examples

exposure_columns <- list("date" = "date", "exposure" = "tmax_C",
                         "geo_unit" = "TOWN20", "geo_unit_grp" = "COUNTY20")
outcome_columns <- list("date" = "date", "outcome" = "daily_deaths",
                        "geo_unit" = "TOWN20", "geo_unit_grp" = "COUNTY20")
time_subset <- list(month = 5:9, year = 2012:2013)
exposure_mat <- make_exposure_matrix(subset(ma_exposure, TOWN20 == "BOSTON"),
                                     exposure_columns, time_subset = time_subset)
#> -- NA values automatically removed
#> strata dt_by = 'day', setting strata as geo_unit:yr:mn:dow
outcomes_tbl <- make_outcome_table(subset(ma_deaths, TOWN20 == "BOSTON"),
                                   outcome_columns, time_subset = time_subset)
#> Missing outcome values introduced by xgrid were set to 0;
#>             assumes that every time in the dataset should have an outcome value
#> strata dt_by = 'day', setting strata as geo_unit:yr:mn:dow
m <- timeseries_1stage_glm(exposure_mat, outcomes_tbl)
#> 
#> crossbasis args for geo_unit  BOSTON :
#> 
#> maxlag: 5 
#> 
#> argvar:
#> List of 2
#>  $ fun  : chr "ns"
#>  $ knots: Named num [1:2] 25.6 31.9
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:2] "50%" "90%"
#> 
#> arglag:
#> List of 2
#>  $ fun  : chr "ns"
#>  $ knots: num [1:2] 0.878 2.095
#> 
#> min_n: 50 
#> 
#> time_trend: annual 
#> n_years (approx): 1.42 
#> df_time for ns(date): 10 
#> add_dow: TRUE 
#> 
#> use_geo_int (multi-zone interactions): FALSE 
#> population offset: none
#> model formula:
#> daily_deaths ~ cb + ns(time_num, df = 10) + dow
#> <environment: 0x17f8a7708>
#>
